## Is it profitable?

**No claim is made, and none should be inferred.** The shipped configuration is an engineering
baseline, not a strategy that has been validated to make money. Some of the project's own measurements
have found losing patterns in its default bots — the point of publishing them is that they are measured
rather than assumed away.

Anyone who tells you their trading bot is profitable without showing you the sample size and the
period is selling something. This project refuses to do that. See the
[Financial Disclaimer](Financial-Disclaimer).

## Do I need MetaTrader 5?

**To run the app: no. To trade through it: yes.**

Without it you get every page, the database, scoring, backtesting, the Lab and the charts. What you
lose is broker bridging — positions, account state and order placement — because those genuinely only
exist at a broker. A second route exists for *data*: 14 provider adapters, several of which need no key
at all.

## Why is my fresh install empty?

**By design.** There is no sample or demo data. The project does not ship fabricated numbers to make a
first screenshot look full, because a fake number in a trading app is indistinguishable from a real one
until it costs someone money.

What you get instead: a setup wizard at `/status/setup` that reports exactly what is and is not
configured, and provider health on `/api/health`.

## Will it place trades without me?

Not unless you configure a bot to. Bots have a mode — `auto` dispatches on the loop, `semi-auto` and
`manual` do not — and a bot with no protocol subscription is never queued at all. That last case is
silent by nature, so there is an audit for it:
`npm --prefix nest run audit:bot-activation`.

## Why did a perfectly good signal not become a trade?

Usually one of: the bot is not subscribed to that protocol; the score did not clear the threshold; a
gate refused it; or the broker cannot trade that symbol *at that size* (a minimum-volume floor is a
common blocker). Every one of those is recorded with a reason — the decision trail exists precisely so
the answer is a lookup rather than a guess.

## Can I run it on Linux or macOS?

Yes, for everything except the bridge. The bridge drives the MetaTrader 5 terminal, which is Windows
software. Trade execution is therefore Windows-only today; everything else is not.

## Is it safe to point at my live account?

**It is not built for that yet, and the project says so rather than leaving you to find out.** A
real-account safety gate — detect a real account, require explicit risk limits and an acknowledgement
before automated trading — is in progress
([#1153](https://github.com/FifeCIC/Trading-Command-Suite/issues/1153)). Until it lands, treat it as a
demo-account tool.

## What does "META.Stack" mean?

**M**odular **E**xpert **T**rading **A**rchitecture. The scoring approach: instead of one monolithic
strategy, a protocol selects a subset of directives, each scoring independently against its own
maximum. Protocol-gated scoring is cheaper than scoring every directive for every symbol, and it is why
a protocol is a first-class object here rather than a config block.

## Something is broken. What do you need from me?

A reproduction: the command or click path, and what you saw instead. Numbers help enormously — "the
score was 71 and the threshold was 75" is fixable; "it did not trade" is not. See
[Contributing](Contributing).

## Why is the codebase so unusual?

It is one person's project with an unusually strict evidence culture: every number in the documentation
is either generated and build-checked, or absent. That produces dense files and long comment blocks —
and it is also why the same class of bug does not come back six times.
